RoboColosseum launches shared real-robot AI evaluation

The initiative advertises more than 100 robots and 10,000 free evaluation hours, distinguishing partial progress from completed tasks.

Humanoids Daily ↗4 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

Shared hardware for researchers

RoboColosseum’s launch involves Hugging Face, BitRobot and Singapore research partners, advertising more than 100 robots, over 140 scenes and 10,000 free academic evaluation hours. Platforms include Unitree G1, SO-101, YAM and Franka, allowing teams to test policies without owning the hardware.

Common protocols, distinct metrics

Open Track evaluates without task-specific adaptation. Fine-tune Track supplies the same 100 demonstrations per task and runs 25 attempts. Reported launch results on G1 covered 625 trials across five policies and five tasks, with no fully completed tasks despite nonzero partial-progress scores.

Making failures inspectable

The initiative uses standardized hardware and trained evaluators and aims to release recordings including failures. Applicants must accept public performance results. The launch reporting does not establish that every recording is already available or that teams must release all model weights and code.
